prompt: The region under $y = 2$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 3$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. The volume of the solid is $k\pi$ cubic units. Find $k$.
hint: Each cross-section perpendicular to the $x$-axis is a disc. What is its radius, and which volume formula adds up discs?

hints.text: Each cross-section perpendicular to the $x$-axis is a disc. What is its radius, and which volume formula adds up discs?
The radius is the height $y = 2$, so the disc method $V = \pi \int_a^b r^2 \, dx$ gives $V = \pi \int_0^3 2^2 \, dx = \pi \int_0^3 4 \, dx$. Evaluate this integral.
The volume of the solid is $V = \pi \cdot 4 \cdot 3 = 12\pi$, so $k = 12$.

explanation: Rotating a horizontal segment at height $2$ sweeps out a cylinder of radius $2$ and length $3$.
The disc method gives the volume $V = \pi \int_0^3 (2)^2 \, dx = \pi [4x]_0^3 = 12\pi$.
So $k = 12$. The cylinder formula agrees, since $\pi r^2 h = \pi \cdot 4 \cdot 3 = 12\pi$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Stack the coins
steps: Picture $3$ units of coins, each a disc of radius $2$ and area $4\pi$.
Volume $=$ area of a coin $\times$ height of the stack $= 4\pi \cdot 3 = 12\pi$.
The integral $\pi \int r^2 \, dx$ is exactly this "area times thickness, summed" idea, and it works even when the radius changes.
